features.title: agent-comms
features.tldr: The handoff-v1 JSON contract agents emit, its validator behind `dadaia reports validate`, and ack-on-consume deletion with a one-day TTL.
features.summary: Agent-to-agent coordination is a JSON handoff under the workspace handoff tree, validated against the packaged handoff-v1 schema, with an HTML report as optional evidence.

features.title: agent-orchestration
features.tldr: Three dd- personas are leaf workers dispatched by the main thread; SDD documents, worktrees and handoffs carry the work, never an orchestration runtime.
features.summary: The role boundary, task-level dispatch contract, evidence flow and install-time model and privilege resolution for the product, software and review personas.

features.title: agentic-entities
features.tldr: One registry names three personas, five deterministic behaviors and two abstract rules; a behavior map assigns each shipped skill and scoped law to an owner.
features.summary: The harness-neutral entity registry, its projected implementations, the universal authored surface and the structural ownership and citation checks that keep agentic law complete.

features.title: agent-evals
features.tldr: The library's own agent evals — two graded tasks run on the candidate wheel and a PyPI baseline by one dispatch-or-schedule workflow.
features.summary: evals/ holds a cold-onboarding task and a block-list-bug task, each graded by a script on the state the agent leaves; .github/workflows/eval.yml runs each three times on a baseline release and on the candidate wheel built from its own checkout, scans every upload for the model secret, and blocks when the candidate drops where the baseline passed.

features.title: public-asset-distribution
features.tldr: Public install stages packaged assets and projects shared law, agents, skills and every registered harness; public doctor reports projection drift.
features.summary: The stage, install and doctor chain that distributes the agentic surface — deterministic staging, rendered personas, whole-folder skills, registry-derived harness files, specs scaffold, projection pruning and privacy checks.

features.title: pypi-distribution
features.tldr: The PyPI package on one version axis, two console-script names, the OIDC pipeline, the wheel contract and the derived docs.
features.summary: dadaia-workspace publishes to PyPI under OIDC trusted publishing from the release-please workflow; release-please owns the version, the CHANGELOG and the tag, and pyproject carries the published floor.

features.title: harness-claude-code
features.tldr: Entry harness with native sub-agent dispatch; reads the root AGENTS.md map natively and reaches skills and personas through per-entry symlinks into .agents/.
features.summary: How Claude Code loads the workspace law, reaches the three dd- personas and the skills, binds a session, and which hook events carry the workspace's behaviours.

features.title: harness-codex
features.tldr: Entry harness on the Codex CLI: native AGENTS.md chain and .agents/skills; .codex/ carries config, hooks, the command policy and persona TOML.
features.summary: Codex reads the root map, the root->cwd AGENTS.md chain and .agents/skills natively; .codex/ holds config.toml, hooks.json, the command-policy rules and the three dd- persona TOMLs transcoded from .agents/agents/.

features.title: harness-copilot
features.tldr: Entry harness on GitHub Copilot CLI — native root AGENTS.md and .agents/skills; .github/ carries agent transcodes and two hook files, bootstrap at start.
features.summary: Copilot reads the universal surface natively; its projection is the three dd- personas as .github/agents/*.agent.md and two hook files answered in Copilot's permissionDecision JSON, and nothing else under .github/.

features.title: harness-cursor
features.tldr: Entry harness on Cursor — native root AGENTS.md and .agents/skills; .cursor/hooks.json gates every tool, injects and reaps at start; persona symlinks.
features.summary: Cursor reads the universal surface natively; its projection is the dd- personas as relative symlinks under .cursor/agents/ and one hooks.json whose gate wrapper answers a deny in Cursor's permission JSON and whose session-start ctx-inject carries the bound context's bootstrap.

features.title: harness-devin
features.tldr: Entry harness on the Devin CLI — native AGENTS.md, .agents/skills and .agents/agents; its one file, .devin/hooks.v1.json, wires gate, injection and reaper.
features.summary: Devin reads the universal surface including the personas natively, so its projection is only .devin/hooks.v1.json, which reads the gate's Claude-compatible envelope without translation.

features.title: harness-kimi-code
features.tldr: Entry harness with an empty projection: reads root AGENTS.md, .agents/skills and .agents/agents natively; user-level hook shims; DADAIA_CONTEXT binds.
features.summary: Kimi Code consumes the universal surface directly and projects nothing into the workspace; its hooks are a managed block and shims in the user-level Kimi home, and its session binds through an exported DADAIA_CONTEXT.

features.title: product-vision
features.tldr: One workspace keeps project repositories inside it and governance outside; each context spans one main repository and any associated repositories.
features.summary: The product paradigm, evidence and coupling principles, and the human and agent paths through one current product truth.

features.title: spec-context-project
features.tldr: One canonical specs tree owned by one main repository, optionally spanning associated repos, bound per session and safe for visible concurrent work.
features.summary: The central unit of dadaia-workspace — one main repository is the sole source of specs, bind, memory, releases and backlog, and associated repositories extend it without a second specs tree.

features.title: capabilities
features.tldr: dadaia capabilities [--json] prints the installed contract: distribution and specs pattern versions, status tokens, the live verbs and harnesses.
features.summary: A read-only verb an agent runs first in a new or upgraded session: a dadaia-capabilities-v3 JSON payload naming the installed distribution version, the canonical specs pattern version and status tokens, the context states, commands and selection contract, the Layer-1 harnesses and every command group with its subcommands, all derived from the live command tree and the harness registry, plus the certify command; the table view is a digest of the same payload.

features.title: Consumer validation gate
features.tldr: A consumer-side agent running the developer's recipe on a real workspace is the release gate; no wheel publishes until every statement reports PASS.
features.summary: The release gate is a consumer-side validation agent running the developer's validation recipe on a real workspace; dadaia certify runs the deterministic journey in a disposable workspace and is necessary, never sufficient.

features.title: context-management
features.tldr: ALIVE/DEAD registry of a main repo plus associated repos; create clones, hooks and ALIVEs; only context bind binds, by env session id, naming the scope.
features.summary: Spec Context Projects and their repos through one registry and the context verbs — create as onboarding level 2, alive, dead, the anchor-first append-only publish of the main repo (baseline), the repo set; one resolution authority whose Bind carries the session's scope and whose scope() maps a path to its repo and zone; bind-driven injection of the constitution, tech stack, catalog, open worktrees and help digests; redaction at the render boundary.

features.title: context-portability
features.tldr: dadaia export writes the workspace's context set to one file; dadaia import registers each unknown context DEAD elsewhere, ready for dadaia context alive.
features.summary: Moving a workspace's Spec Context Projects to another workspace — export writes .dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json (spec-contexts-export-v1) after refreshing ALIVE branches; import accepts only that schema, registers unknown names DEAD through the same guarded insert as context create, and names the alive command that restores each.

features.title: cross-platform-portability
features.tldr: Linux, macOS and Windows through one platform capability seam carrying the venv layout, Python hooks and cross-OS CI legs.
features.summary: dadaia_workspace/core/platform.py is the single capability source — two flags, the venv scripts directory and the executable suffix — read by the modules that build venv paths; no port, adapter pair or file lock exists for portability.

features.title: server-registry
features.tldr: Dev-server port registry with TTL and PID tracking so parallel sessions never collide — one stdlib skill script over one JSON state file; no CLI verb.
features.summary: python3 .agents/skills/dd-cli-library/scripts/registry.py keeps .dadaia/states/server_registry.json — per-project ports with TTL and PID, deterministic next-port allocation, idempotent register, release, stale sweep and a read-only scan of unregistered OS listeners.

features.title: specs-migration
features.tldr: specs init establishes canon and gitflow; specs upgrade reaches pattern 12; migrate updates the context registry.
features.summary: The persisted-state upgrade verbs: specs init scaffolds or upgrades a dadaia tree and preserves a foreign tree in specs-bkp; specs upgrade runs the supported migration and repair set before stamping pattern 12; migrate updates the context registry atomically.

features.title: workspace-doctor
features.tldr: dadaia doctor, the one compliance check — workspace, specs, ledgers; one line per finding, exit 1 with a fix line; --fix holds slop, expiry acts by zone class.
features.summary: dadaia doctor runs three sections (workspace walk, specs rules, ledger checks) from one rule record, prints each non-canonical finding as one line with a runnable fix, exits 1 on any error-class finding and reports no score; --fix is the reaper, seeding missing level-1 core, moving slop into a held zone and taking a TTL-expired entry by its zone's class — an output entry held, an ephemeral one deleted.

features.title: workspace-init
features.tldr: Level 1 — uvx dadaia-workspace init [DIR] provisions venv, zones, law, one harness; re-init upgrades; --repo adds level 2; next step from one ordered step list.
features.summary: dadaia init fills one plan from flags or prompts, provisions the venv and workspace tree, seeds state, and invokes the install path that stages current public assets before projection; re-init upgrades, and one ordered real-state step list drives onboarding guidance.

features.title: audits-canon
features.tldr: An audit runs bug-history, spec-compliance and memory-drift pillars over one measured window and stores schema-valid findings until terminal disposition.
features.summary: The three-pillar audit, reproducible finding evidence, terminal disposition vocabulary, single remediation release and atomic archive close.

features.title: backlog-ledger
features.tldr: The operator's demand queue: BACKLOG.json active[] plus one histo record per exit; backlog.py writes it, dadaia doctor judges bound subjects.
features.summary: The backlog ledger — specs/backlog/BACKLOG.json holding every live entry in active[], and _archive/backlog_histo.jsonl holding one terminal record per exited slug; backlog.py is the one writer and validator, and the doctor's ledgers section resolves each entry's bound intents.

features.title: bug-ledger
features.tldr: BUGS.jsonl stores one lean current record per confirmed defect; its writer persists registration and resolution facts while git owns derived history.
features.summary: The bug record grammar, confirmation and privacy boundary, terminal transitions, persisted fix lineage, archival and candidate integration.

features.title: release-lifecycle
features.tldr: One live release grows through closed-scope candidates; _RELEASE.json holds current phase, milestones and a lean append-only narrative.
features.summary: Candidate birth, approval, task and job structure, phase transitions, authoritative memory drift, closure records, open-bug ship authorization and archival.

features.title: sdd-gate-v3
features.tldr: No-lock enforcement combines root-entry hygiene and SDD write policy before tools, then applies branch, specs-canon and privacy checks at push.
features.summary: The two-policy pre-tool gate, path classes and bind scope, fail-open boundaries, one-fix refusal shape and range-scoped git publication chokepoint.

features.title: worktrees
features.tldr: Repository changes are isolated in canonical plain, release, task, backlog or hotfix worktrees and land by worktree.py merge after the gate for that tree shape.
features.summary: The worktree grammar, recorded bases, RED/implementation separation, one reviewed job or plain-change gate, merge cleanup and closure holds.
